summary: web3-eth-utils 1.0.3 installs a reverse shell to 45.138.12.177:8089 via extconf.rb
details: The gem declares a native extension at ext/req_throttle_mini/extconf.rb but ships no C/C++ sources — the directory contains only the extconf.rb script and ends with a two-line create_makefile('web3_eth_utils_native') stub. RubyGems auto-runs extconf.rb during `gem install`. Before the stub, the script base64-decodes an opaque string and passes it to eval() inside a double-forked, detached child process. The decoded payload opens a TCP socket to 45.138.12.177:8089 and pipes it to /bin/sh in a reconnect loop, giving the remote endpoint an interactive shell on the installer's machine. The script gates execution behind sandbox/CI/analysis evasion checks (in_ci?, ephemeral_host?, generated_user?, analysis_path?, machine_age_ok?, dev_signals?) and a 1200+rand(1200) second sleep, so the backdoor fires on real developer workstations while suppressing itself in automated analysis environments. lib/web3_eth_utils.rb is a small benign stub, consistent with a typosquat/dependency-confusion decoy wrapping an install-time dropper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
